ci._comment_collect: Start the production build (not dev server) so scores reflect what users see. `next start` on port 3002 matches Playwright + other local tooling. 3 runs per URL to damp noise; the median is what LHCI asserts against. Only public routes are audited — every admin route requires a Supabase session cookie that CI doesn't carry.

collect._comment_cmd: Invoke `next start` directly via `pnpm exec` rather than `pnpm run start -- --port 3002` because the nested `--` argument forwarding gets miscounted on pnpm 9: `next start` sees `--port` as the project directory and exits with 'Invalid project directory'. Dropping the indirection makes the port flag unambiguous.
collect.startServerCommand: pnpm run build && pnpm exec next start -p 3002

ci._comment_assert: Thresholds split into two tiers: `error` for load-bearing properties that a regression on is a real user-facing bug. After Session 12 landed the initial threshold set (warn-only for performance + best-practices), Session 13 pinned both to `error` tier based on the measured baseline scores from PR #21's LHCI run (all four categories passed comfortably above the warn thresholds). The baseline run measurements told us we had at least 15 points of headroom to `error`-tier tightening without flaking — any future regression below these floors is a real signal worth blocking. Floors use a conservative 5-10 point buffer below baseline so minor noise doesn't flake a PR. We intentionally do NOT use `lighthouse:recommended` as a base preset — that layer asserts minScore on per-audit signals like `non-composited-animations`, many of which return NaN on static landing pages and trip the gate for the wrong reason.

upload._comment: temporary-public-storage uploads the JSON report to a free LHCI CDN with a 7-day TTL. Each PR gets a URL to the full Lighthouse report attached to the job log — no LHCI server to run. Fine for our volume; revisit if we ship an internal dashboard for perf trend lines.
